items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (buildWindowClause, validateWindowName, WindowDefinitionConfig, WindowFrameBoundaryType). Dialect edits match local style, e.g. `const windowSql = buildWindowClause(windows);`. Tests and type-tests are descriptive. No cryptic names in what is visible.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Good: one shared buildWindowClause and validateWindowName live in window.ts (377 lines). But the ~20-line .window() body, including the SelectionProxyHandler callback branch, is copied into all five select.ts files. That goes beyond the 'thin method' the conventions ask for.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: validateWindowName runs at the .window() entry point. Hidden tests covering the ntile/nthValue, preceding/following and from-after-to frame checks all pass (F2P 130/130). Positional numbers are not bound as params; the tests show `params: []`. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: `export * from './window.ts'`, an optional `windows?: WindowDefinitionConfig[]` on all five *SelectConfig types, and the same .window() on pg/mysql/sqlite/singlestore/gel. windowSql is undefined when unused, so existing SQL is unchanged (P2P 566/566).
